current_answer: Open Technology Fund’s Internet Freedom Fund is a rolling global route for a defined internet-freedom project: individuals can apply, and published awards range from USD 10,000 to USD 900,000 for up to 24 months. This is not a general personal grant: the work must fit the fund, awards are performance-based contracts, and applicants in sanctioned jurisdictions are excluded. Separately, Cloudflare now publishes a typical review estimate, product caps, exclusions, and automatic-billing terms for its startup credits, but its Tier 3 still says both “self-funded” and “funded within the last 12 months.”

catalogue_card.question: A USD 10,000–900,000 grant is open to individuals. Is your project actually in scope?
catalogue_card.text: Open Technology Fund accepts rolling applications globally for defined internet-freedom work. The range is real; a general personal grant is not. Check scope, sanctions restrictions, and the deliverables-based contract before you draft.

summary: Open Technology Fund’s Internet Freedom Fund accepts rolling applications from individuals and organisations for defined internet-freedom projects.
OTF publishes awards of USD 10,000–900,000 for up to 24 months; its stated ideal request is USD 50,000–200,000 for six to 12 months.
Applicants first submit a Concept Note. OTF says it replies in about 6–8 weeks; competitive applicants are invited to a full proposal.
Awards are performance-based contracts paid against deliverables, not unrestricted personal funding.
Cloudflare now publishes review, cap, exclusion, and billing terms, but its self-funded Tier 3 and recent-funding condition remain unresolved.
uncertainty: Open Technology Fund is not general personal support: only a defined internet-freedom project within its remit can compete, and its published award range is not a promised or typical award.
Open Technology Fund excludes applicants in countries subject to applicable United States trade restrictions or export sanctions.
Cloudflare Tier 3 still pairs “bootstrapped or self-funded” with a programme-wide “funded within the last 12 months” condition; the issuer has not reconciled the terms.
Cloudflare’s review estimate is not an approval promise, and credits can have product caps, exclusions, overages, and post-expiry billing.
DigitalOcean does not publish a fixed direct-applicant award, country-availability map, review time, or applicant-specific GPU-credit outcome.
Individual-grant coverage is still narrow and not a worldwide inventory.
